# SPRAWL V2: the wired predecessor of MËSH {background-image="pictures/goat_farm.jpeg" background-opacity="0.45"}

## SPRAWL → SPRAWL V2

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**SPRAWL** (2019/20)

- Central server: routing, mixing, spatialisation
- Access points on a wired LAN
- Control via OSC [@wright2003opensound]
:::
::: {.column width="50%" .fragment}
**SPRAWL V2** (2024)

- **A speaker at every access point**
- New hardware, **no central server**
- Fully connected mesh, but every link is a cable
:::
::::

::: prose
The original SPRAWL used a client–server architecture: a central server handled audio routing, mixing and spatialisation, and performers connected through access points on a wired LAN. Audio from each access point went to the server, was processed and redistributed to the other performers and the spatialisation system, while OSC handled control such as levels, routing and spatialisation. A pre-version in late 2023 in Germany almost had this, but its speakers were still placed conservatively. SPRAWL V2, in 2024, put a speaker at every access point, updated the hardware and removed the central server, connecting the access points in a fully connected mesh. That is stable and low-latency, but it still depends on wired connections between all components.
:::

## Goat Farm Arts Center, Atlanta · Fall 2024

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **12** access points, one musician each
- Student-built SPRAWL V2 programs
  - spatialised granular synthesis
  - graphic scores for audience and players
- Some access points open to the audience
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![A SPRAWL V2 access point: drum into microphone, interface, system.](pictures/goat_farm.jpeg){.photo .ph}
:::
::::

::: prose
In fall 2024 SPRAWL V2 was used at The Goat Farm Arts Center in Atlanta. Twelve access points were set up, each with a musician playing their own instrument into the system. The concert consisted of student-created programs ranging from real-time spatialised granular synthesis to a graphic score visible to audience and musicians. At the access point shown, the drum is picked up by a microphone into the audio interface and fed into the system; other access points let the audience play along.
:::

## SuperCollider Symposium, DC · Spring 2025

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
![Workshop at the SuperCollider Symposium.](pictures/scsymp_workshop.jpg){.photo .ph}
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
- Workshop: techniques for distributed systems
- Fully connected mesh; attendees designed the processing for their access point
- **5 access points**
- **10-hour drive** in a midsize car

::: {.fragment}
→ this is what we set out to fix
:::
:::
::::

::: prose
After being taught in the classroom in fall 2024, SPRAWL V2 went to Washington, DC in spring 2025 for a workshop at the SuperCollider Symposium. The workshop covered techniques for working with SPRAWL V2 and, more generally, with distributed performance systems; attendees designed the audio processing for their own access point in the mesh. Bringing five access points meant a ten-hour drive from Atlanta in a midsize vehicle. That trip motivated MËSH.
:::
